subject: Clarify: default capture window for request/response, derived outputs, and deletion mechanics
messages:
From: Alyssa Moore <alyssa@brightbank.com>

Cc: security-team@brightbank.com
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clarifications on default log capture and deletion for POC

Hi Chloe / Marissa,

We're kicking off the BrightBank POC next week and the security team asked for a concise explanation of what Redwood stores by default. A few specific questions they want clarified before we go live:

- For the hosted API, what is the default retention window for request/response logs (timestamps + raw text)?
- Do user prompts and model outputs get treated differently (i.e., are outputs considered derivatives and retained longer)?
- For streaming sessions / KV-cache-backed sessions, are partial responses or intermediate cache snapshots persisted?
- If BrightBank requests account-wide purge (subject access / deletion), what is the SLA and how do you prove deletion to an auditor?
- Residency: if we select US-only, are backups or tombstones ever replicated outside the selected region?

If you can point to the specific runbook or share the minimal wording we can put in our security questionnaire, that would be great.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Moore
Security Lead, BrightBank

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list.

Short answers up front (I’ll loop Karthik in for product-level detail and the runbook link):
- Default request/response retention: 30 days.
- Prompts (raw user input) vs outputs (model-generated content): prompts are treated as request artifacts; outputs are classified as generated derivatives and handled under a separate eval/derivative policy (details below).
- Streaming / KV cache: streaming payloads are ephemeral by default unless you specifically enable session tracing; KV caches are transient and not written to persistent long-term storage.
- Purge SLA: standard account-wide purge requests are handled within 5 business days; proof of deletion (audit log and deletion report) can be provided.
- Region: if you choose US-only for the POC, data is stored solely in US regions; backups and tombstones remain in-region unless you opt into cross-region replication for DR.

Karthik — can you confirm the more precise definitions (what we consider a derivative vs request artifact) and attach the runbook snippet we give customers? Alyssa — copying Marissa for any contract/exception asks.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Alyssa — detailed breakdown to use in your questionnaire: please feel free to paste directly.

1) Default retention windows (hosted API, no special flags)
   - Request/response logs (raw request text, model response text, timestamps, routing metadata): default retention = 30 calendar days.
   - Prompt artifacts (the initial user prompt or system prompt text as received): stored as part of the request record and follow the 30-day retention. Prompts are not double-stored as separate long-lived objects unless you enable prompt-archive in Console.
   - Generated outputs (model completions, suggestions): considered "derivative artifacts." By default they are retained for 90 days only if you opt into "derivative retention" for quality/regression monitoring. For POC customers we keep derivative retention off by default; enabling it is an opt-in that we document and you can control by model/route.

2) Streaming & KV cache behavior
   - Streaming responses are buffered for delivery only; by default we only persist the final completion text in the request/response log at the end of the session.
   - KV cache entries (prefix caches, KV context) are in-memory transient structures; we persist snapshots only if you enable session recording. Session recording is off by default for hosted customers.

3) Deletion & purge mechanics
   - Customer-initiated account purge: open a support case referencing the account id and the scope (e.g., requests, derivatives). We perform an internal purge that removes active records and schedules tombstone and index cleanup.
   - SLA: 5 business days for the primary purge process; full propagation including index compaction/tombstone expiry may take up to 30 additional calendar days depending on shard compaction cycles.
   - Proof of deletion: we provide a deletion certificate (signed) plus an audit export showing pre/post counts and the purge request ticket id. For regulated customers we can arrange a data destruction attestation (SOW add-on).

4) Residency and backups
   - If you pick US-only region at account setup we ensure all primary, backup, and tombstone storage stays within US regions. Cross-region replication is opt-in and disabled by default.

5) Edge cases & notes
   - Redaction/filtering: PII redaction can be applied on ingest via API flags or Console routes; redacted elements are replaced before storage.
   - Telemetry/operational logs: low-level operational traces (runtime telemetry) are stored separately from request/response logs and adhere to a different retention policy; we can include those if you need for an audit.

Runbook links and attachments: I’ve attached our internal "Data Purge Runbook" (excerpt) and a short POC checklist you can share.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Data Governance

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups for the security questionnaire:

- The 30-day default for request/response: is that configurable per-account or per-route? We may need an exception for a small pilot where we want 7-day retention.
- For the deletion certificate: what format is the certificate in, and is it signed by Redwood legal/ops? Our auditor will expect a signed artifact with a timestamp and ticket number.

If you can confirm those two points I can close out the questionnaire and move the POC into procurement.

Best,
Alyssa

Alyssa — quick answers:
- Retention config: retention window can be configured at the account level; we can set a 7-day window for the pilot. I’ll note that changes to retention are recorded in the audit trail.
- Deletion certificate: we produce a signed PDF certificate (signed by our Data Governance lead) that includes the purge ticket id, timestamps, pre/post record counts, and a hash of the deletion report. That meets standard audit requirements; if BrightBank needs a bespoke attestation we can escalate to SOW.

Marissa — please help with the procurement notes and confirm whether the 7-day retention pilot needs a formal exception or if we can onboard under standard terms.

Thanks all — Alyssa, I’ve attached the runbook excerpt Karthik referenced and a one‑page pilot checklist.
